subject: POC: Delta Commerce trial scope, acceptance criteria, and integration sprint

Subject: POC: Delta Commerce trial scope, acceptance criteria, and integration sprint

Alex — great call earlier. Thanks for carving out time. Quick written recap and the proposed next steps so we have a shared place to iterate. I attached a one‑page success criteria workbook (delta_poc_success_criteria.xlsx).

Summary of what we covered
- Objectives: measure latency and cost per 1k inference for the product recommendations flow; validate streaming quality for conversational agent use; confirm tool/function calling for order lookups.
- Success metrics (proposed): 99th perc latency < 250ms for 4k token contexts, average cost per 1k tokens < $X (TBD after RTT), recommendation precision uplift >= 6% over baseline.
- Scope: 2× API routes (generate/chat), 1× embedding route for similarity search, streaming enabled for chat path, and a test tool call endpoint that can reach your order service sandbox.

Proposed timeline (draft)
- Week 0 (May 8): kickoff + environment & keys exchange.
- Week 1–2: SDK integration + basic routing; embedding indexing of 10k SKUs; smoke test.
- Week 3: full streaming evaluation and tool-calling tests with your sandbox.
- Week 4: acceptance run and PDF signoff.

Owners (Redwood)
- Marissa: POC program & coordination (me)
- Ben: runtime/SDK and endpoint guidance
- Karthik: quantization and performance tuning / Dedicated capacity advice
- Soojin: instrumentation, eval harness, and metrics dashboard

Next actions for Delta (please confirm or adjust)
1) Confirm acceptance criteria in the attached sheet and return with any changes by EOD May 5.
2) Share sandbox API host and a service account for our test tool-calling by May 8.
3) Procurement contact for SOW execution (cc Procurement Team if possible).

Attachments: delta_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (single-sheet, criteria + metric baselines)

If that all looks good, I'll lock a 30‑minute kickoff for next Tue (May 8) at 10am PT.

—Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of small edits from our side and a couple of questions: 

1) Success metric change: for recommendation uplift we'd prefer a relative lift vs rolling 30‑day baseline (so we can account for seasonality). Can you reflect that in row 4 of the workbook?
2) Streaming: we need to know whether the SDK will deliver partial tokens via SSE/websocket (we prefer websocket).
3) Tool-calling: our order lookup expects a signed JWT per call; can Redwood support a per-request signed assertion or do we need to proxy through a token exchange endpoint?

Procurement: looping you in. Our legal will review the SOW and likely send redlines — LM will lead on that. LM, can you flag any non-standard timelines we should be aware of?

Also, DocuSign is usually best for us. Here’s the procurement contact: procure@deltacorp.com.

Alex — quick technical clarifications from the runtime/SDK side (copying the bits most relevant to your engineering team):

- SDK streaming: Redwood SDK supports both SSE and websocket streaming for tokens. Websocket is recommended for interactive UIs; our websocket client pushes partial tokens as they become available and exposes an onChunk callback.
- Auth / tool-calls: we support two patterns: 
  1) Per-request signed JWT you provide (our server will forward it as-is to the tool endpoint), or
  2) Token-exchange proxy where Redwood mints short-lived service tokens via your OIDC endpoint (we can walk through your security folks).
- Endpoints: sample routes you can expect in the trial:
  - POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate (sync generation)
  - POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream (websocket & SSE compatible)
  - POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
  - POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall/order-lookup (used in tool-calling smoke tests)
- SDKs: we’ll hand you a pre-release node + python package for the trial. The node package has a sample websocket helper and a tool‑calling wrapper.

I attached a small Postman collection for quick smoke tests (delta_postman_collection.json) — it includes the sample routes above and examples for JWT vs proxy flows.

If you foresee needing dedicated capacity during the acceptance run (we can run the acceptance window on shared first), flag that ASAP — Karthik can scope the uplift and time to provision.

—Ben
